newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite radio official.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite radio official.

text.p: Gunmen killed a Shi'ite Moslem state radio journalist in Pakistan's central province of Punjab on Monday, police said.
They said Shamsuddin Haider, a programme producer of the state-run Radio Pakistan, was shot at his home by two gunmen in the southern Punjab town of Bahawalpur.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, but the police said they suspected the killing to be the latest in a series of violent attacks by rival militant groups of the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite sects of Islam.

Haider had been receiving threatening telephone calls from unknown people about radio programmes broadcast by the Bahawalpur radio station during a Shi'ite commemorative festival last month, his family members said.

A long-running feud between the Sunni and Shi'ite militant groups cost at least 170 lives in Pakistan last year and more than 70 people, including religious scholars and doctors, have been killed this year.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan. Sunnis dominate Pakistan's population of more than 130 million, while Shi'ites comprise about 15 percent but are the majority in neighbouring Iran.
